slides.title: What part of you have you been hiding, even from yourself?

body.text: This is your question for today. Keep it in mind during the games.
Three games tonight: standing, guarded, pinned. Win one and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run the same one again.
Skill Learning Objective (SLO): Entering, for both players.
Both players stand facing each other, not gripped, starting to hand fight.
Collect three touches. A touch is a hand behind your partner's knee or an underhook. Any mix counts. Only after three touches can you try for a closed-hand connection.

items: Whoever collects three touches and then connects first wins, closing his hands anywhere on his partner's body from shoulders to ankles.

body.text: Side Half Guard, Clear Hands to Get Under Elbow
SLO: Arriving for the top player, Leaving for the bottom player.
The bottom player is on his side in half guard, hands fully out on the top player. The top player is inside.

Top player: clear the bottom player's hands and get under one or both elbows, then connect your hands. Bottom player: keep your hands on the top player to deny that spot, and close your legs around his waist.

items: The top player wins by connecting his hands under at least one elbow.
The bottom player wins by closing his legs around the top player's waist.

body.text: SLO: Controlling for the top player, Leaving for the bottom player.
The bottom player is on his back. The top player is chest to chest on top of him.
Top player: hold chest to chest and keep the bottom player there. Bottom player: push the top player off and get your legs back in front.

items: The top player has no time limit. He holds the pin.
The bottom player wins by pushing the top player off and getting his legs back in front.

slides.question: In Introductory Pin Game, what wins it for the top player?

options.text: The top player has no time limit. He holds the pin.
options.feedback: That is the win condition, and nothing else scores.
Not part of the Paths yet. Entering and Arriving are the two steps here, and neither one ends in a finish. The path leads you into a pin, not a finish.
Never. Everyone goes light, and the tap always stops it right away, every time.
